title: 725. 1-bit and 2-bit Characters

examples.explanation: The encoding splits as 10 then 0, so the final symbol uses one bit.
The only split is 11 then 10, leaving a two-bit tail.
A lone zero is a one-bit symbol.

hints: A 1 always starts a two-bit symbol and consumes the next bit; a 0 stands alone.
Walk from the front jumping 1 or 2 steps and see where you land relative to the last index.
The answer is true exactly when the walk ends on the final position, not before it.
